look_here_first: Find a thorny short shoot and FLIP a mature leaf. Gum bumelia has alternate simple smooth-edged leaves, generally glossy green above and thickly woolly/grayish to tawny beneath, often clustered on short spur shoots. The leaves are not genuinely whorled. Then seek tiny whitish flower clusters or dark oblong fruits with hard seed.

genus_recognition.habitus: Woody native Sapotaceae shrub or small tree, armed and unarmed shoots possible. Twigs sometimes end in stout, rigid spine-like short-shoot tips.
genus_recognition.node_leaf: Leaves are alternate, but can APPEAR clustered or whorled where several arise on a short spur; distinguish the full shoot from a single cropped leaf tuft.
genus_recognition.leaf: Entire leathery elliptic to obovate simple blades, darker glossier above, varying pale/woolly below, especially young leaves; underside hair may persist or thin with age and different infraspecific forms.
genus_recognition.flower_and_fruit: Tiny cream-white clustered flowers at short shoots, later dark blue-black oblong fleshy fruits usually with one large glossy hard seed.
genus_recognition.latex: Sticky gum/latex only as a supporting field cue where already exposed; do not cut living stems solely to test.

field_id_sequence: 1. Find a FULL shoot and observe the alternate leaf attachments plus congested short spur branches; do not infer an opposite/whorled leaf arrangement from a spur tuft.
2. Inspect mature upper versus lower leaf surfaces on the SAME leaf. The underside's pale to tawny woolly hairs, when present, strongly support S. lanuginosum.
3. Look along older shoots for rigid sharp spur tips; thorns are useful but may be absent from part of an individual plant.
4. Check small flowers clustered on spurs in spring/summer or elongated blue-black berries in late summer/fall; avoid fruit-color-only ID.
5. Compare persimmon and hollies using persistent fruit calyx, fruit type, twig spines, and abaxial pubescence; if no underside or shoot is documented, stay at genus/family level.

lookalike_matrix.Sideroxylon lanuginosum: Often densely woolly/tawny/gray below, especially young leaves; older leaves may be less hairy
lookalike_matrix.Sideroxylon celastrinum: Usually much smoother/glabrous underside and smaller blades; native farther south in Texas (separate related taxon)
lookalike_matrix.Diospyros texana: No similarly dense woolly bumelia underside; hairs/variation may occur in young growth
lookalike_matrix.Ilex decidua: Usually not densely woolly; deciduous leaves often with fine marginal teeth

lookalike_matrix.Sideroxylon lanuginosum: Entire alternate leaves clustered on spur branches with some short shoots ending in rigid spines
lookalike_matrix.Sideroxylon celastrinum: Similar thorny Sideroxylon; underside texture is a higher-value split
lookalike_matrix.Diospyros texana: Thornless alternate leaves; smooth gray peeling older bark is often distinctive
lookalike_matrix.Ilex decidua: Alternate thin leaves, often finely crenate, generally unarmed

lookalike_matrix.Sideroxylon lanuginosum: Blackish oblong fleshy fruit, one hard glossy seed; stems sometimes spiny
lookalike_matrix.Sideroxylon celastrinum: Dark berries too—cannot separate by fruit color alone
lookalike_matrix.Diospyros texana: Fleshy black persimmon with prominent persistent cup-shaped calyx
lookalike_matrix.Ilex decidua: Clustered small orange-red/orange drupes persisting on bare shoots, not oblong blue-black bumelia fruit

lookalike_matrix.Sideroxylon lanuginosum: Woolly underside + hard spur tip + alternate entire leaves
lookalike_matrix.Sideroxylon celastrinum: Smooth abaxial and southerly range; provenance alone not ID
lookalike_matrix.Diospyros texana: Usually lacking hard spines and with very different fruit calyx

photo_cautions: Spur leaves may appear whorled despite alternate true shoot phyllotaxis.
Thorn tips and leaf hairs can vary by age and geography; one absence is not a species exclusion.
Do NOT invent arrow coordinates on botanical-garden pictures. Add arrows after actually viewing each installed file.
Only use UT Austin and Trees and Shrubs Online examples as hyperlinked study references unless rights are independently cleared.
